full_text_en:
Gaochun County Civil Affairs Bureau v. Wang Changsheng, Lü Fang, and Tianan Insurance Jiangsu Branch — dispute over personal injury compensation arising from a traffic accident

[Ruling Summary]

In a personal injury compensation case arising from a traffic accident, where the deceased victim is a city-dwelling vagrant and beggar with no means of livelihood, and after the public security authorities have published a notice but failed to locate any close relatives, if the civil affairs department files a civil lawsuit as the plaintiff demanding that the compensation obligor bear liability for compensation, because the civil affairs department is not a compensation claimant as provided by law, has no civil rights-obligations relationship with the case, and its statutory duties do not include representing or substituting for city-dwelling vagrants and beggars with no means of livelihood in filing civil lawsuits, the civil affairs department is not a proper litigation subject in the case, and its lawsuit should be dismissed according to law.

Plaintiff: Gaochun County Civil Affairs Bureau, Jiangsu Province, domiciled at Beiyi Road, Chunxi Town, Gaochun County, Jiangsu Province.

Legal Representative: Zhang Zhaoxia, Director of the Bureau.

Defendant: Wang Changsheng, male, 54 years old, driver, residing at Youzishan Village, Dongba Town, Gaochun County.

Defendant: Lü Fang, female, 29 years old, staff member of the Bill Center, China Construction Bank, Jiangsu Branch, residing at Suojin Village, Xuanwu District, Nanjing.

Defendant: Tianan Insurance Co., Ltd., Jiangsu Branch, domiciled at Huawei Building, Shigu Road, Nanjing.

Person in Charge: Yuan Xuelou, General Manager of the Branch.

The plaintiff, Gaochun County Civil Affairs Bureau, Jiangsu Province (hereinafter referred to as Gaochun Civil Affairs Bureau), filed a lawsuit with the Gaochun County People's Court, Jiangsu Province, against the defendants Wang Changsheng, Lü Fang, and Tianan Insurance Co., Ltd., Jiangsu Branch (hereinafter referred to as Tianan Insurance Jiangsu Branch) concerning a dispute over personal injury compensation arising from a traffic accident.

Plaintiff's Allegations: At approximately 19:30 on April 2, 2005, the defendants Wang Changsheng and Lü Fang, due to a traffic accident, caused the death on the spot of an unidentified man aged between 60 and 70. On April 20, 2005, the Traffic Patrol Detachment of the Gaochun County Public Security Bureau issued Traffic Accident Determination No. 2005023, determining that Wang Changsheng and Lü Fang bore equal liability for the traffic accident, and the unidentified deceased victim bore no liability for the accident. After the accident, on April 4, 2005, the Traffic Patrol Detachment published a corpse identification notice in the *Nanjing Daily*. As no one claimed the body, the unidentified man's body was cremated on April 21 of the same year, and his ashes were temporarily kept by the Gaochun County Funeral Home. The motor vehicles driven by Wang Changsheng and Lü Fang were both insured with the defendant Tianan Insurance Jiangsu Branch under third-party liability insurance, with liability limits of RMB 50,000 and RMB 200,000 respectively. The plaintiff, as a specialized agency responsible for providing relief to society's vagrants and beggars, undertook the work of providing relief to society's vagrants and beggars, and its work duties should also include supporting the assertion of rights by society's vagrants and beggars. In this case, the unidentified deceased victim's right to life and health should be protected by law. The man died in a traffic accident, and the plaintiff undertook the relevant handling matters, so it has the right to claim compensation from the three defendants for his death. The Gaochun County People's Procuratorate, as a legal supervisory body, also supported the plaintiff in filing a lawsuit for damages according to law, and for this purpose issued Procuratorial Suggestion No. Ning Gao Jian Min Xing Jian [2006] 12. The plaintiff requested that Tianan Insurance Jiangsu Branch be ordered to pay RMB 166,331 within the limits of compulsory third-party liability insurance.

Defendants' Joint Defense: The civil affairs bureau provides relief to society's vagrants and beggars according to its duties. The relationship formed between them is an administrative legal relationship, not a civil legal relationship. The plaintiff, Gaochun Civil Affairs Bureau, in claiming personal injury compensation from a traffic accident on behalf of the victim in this case, has no legal basis, does not have civil subject qualifications, and does not have the right of action in this case. The cremation and storage of the victim's body in this case were paid services; the funeral expenses have already been actually paid by the defendants. Gaochun Civil Affairs Bureau has not provided evidence that it actually provided relief to the victim in this case, and its claim lacks factual basis. The defendants requested that the lawsuit of Gaochun Civil Affairs Bureau be dismissed.

Facts Found by the Court of First Instance (Gaochun County People's Court):

At approximately 19:30 on April 2, 2005, the defendant Wang Changsheng, driving a three-wheeled transport vehicle with license plate number Su AQ0128, was traveling south along Shuangwang Road. When he reached the 4KM section, he collided with an unidentified man aged between 60 and 70, knocking him into the east motor vehicle lane. At that moment, the defendant Lü Fang, driving a car with license plate number Su AAV822 from south to north through the same section, ran over the man's body, causing his instantaneous death. On April 20, 2005, the Traffic Patrol Detachment of the Gaochun County Public Security Bureau issued Traffic Accident Determination No. 2005023, determining that Wang Changsheng and Lü Fang bore equal liability for the traffic accident, and the unidentified deceased victim bore no liability. After the accident, on April 4, 2005, the Traffic Patrol Detachment published a corpse identification notice in the *Nanjing Daily*. As no one claimed the body, the unidentified man's body was cremated on April 21 of the same year, and his ashes were temporarily kept by the Gaochun County Funeral Home. Wang Changsheng's three-wheeled vehicle (Su AQ0128) and Lü Fang's car (Su AAV822) were both insured with the defendant Tianan Insurance Jiangsu Branch under third-party liability insurance, with liability limits of RMB 50,000 and RMB 200,000 respectively.

Additionally, it was found that the work duties of the plaintiff, Gaochun Civil Affairs Bureau, include providing relief to society's vagrants and beggars.

Issue in Dispute: Whether the plaintiff Gaochun Civil Affairs Bureau is a proper litigation subject in this case and whether it can claim compensation from the defendants Wang Changsheng, Lü Fang, and Tianan Insurance Jiangsu Branch for the death of the unidentified deceased victim.

Opinion of the Court of First Instance (Gaochun County People's Court):

The plaintiff, Gaochun Civil Affairs Bureau, as the specialized government agency responsible for providing relief to society's vagrants and beggars, only has an administrative legal relationship with the unidentified deceased victim in this case, not a civil legal relationship. Therefore, it is not a proper civil litigation plaintiff in this case and has no right to claim personal injury compensation from the traffic accident against the defendants Wang Changsheng, Lü Fang, and Tianan Insurance Jiangsu Branch for the death of the unidentified man.

Accordingly, on December 4, 2006, the Gaochun County People's Court ruled as follows:

The lawsuit filed by the plaintiff Gaochun County Civil Affairs Bureau is dismissed.

Plaintiff's Appeal (Gaochun Civil Affairs Bureau):

Dissatisfied with the ruling of the first instance, Gaochun Civil Affairs Bureau appealed to the Nanjing Intermediate People's Court. Its main reasons were: 1. The civil affairs bureau is responsible for providing relief to society's vagrants and beggars with no means of livelihood. This relief duty is not only reflected in providing living security for such persons but should also include implementing judicial relief by filing lawsuits on their behalf when they suffer personal harm; 2. Although the appellant is an administrative organ, in this case it actually undertook the funeral and cremation arrangements for the unidentified deceased victim, so it has not only an administrative legal relationship but also a certain civil legal relationship with the unidentified man; 3. The appellant's claim for compensation for death compensation and funeral expenses complies with the relevant judicial interpretations of the Supreme People's Court. In this case, the unidentified deceased victim indeed has no relatives to assert civil rights on his behalf. If the appellant's civil litigation subject qualification is denied, it would objectively allow the tortfeasor to evade the civil compensation liability it should bear, contrary to fundamental legal principles. The appellant requested the court of second instance to set aside the original ruling.

Response of Appellees:

The appellee Wang Changsheng, after being legally summoned by the Nanjing Intermediate People's Court, did not appear in court and did not submit a defense.

The appellees Lü Fang and Tianan Insurance Jiangsu Branch jointly argued: The civil affairs bureau provides relief to society's vagrants and beggars according to its duties. The relationship formed between them is an administrative legal relationship, not a civil legal relationship. The appellant, Gaochun Civil Affairs Bureau, in claiming personal injury compensation from a traffic accident on behalf of the victim in this case, has no legal basis, does not have civil subject qualifications, and does not have the right of action in this case. The cremation and storage of the victim's body in this case were paid services; the funeral expenses have already been actually paid by the appellees. Gaochun Civil Affairs Bureau has not provided evidence that it actually provided relief to the victim in this case, and its claim lacks factual basis. The original ruling was correct, and the appellees requested that Gaochun Civil Affairs Bureau's appeal be dismissed and the original ruling be affirmed.

Facts Found by the Court of Second Instance (Nanjing Intermediate People's Court):

The court of second instance confirmed the facts found by the court of first instance.

Issue in Dispute in the Second Instance:

The issue to be resolved in the second instance remained whether the appellant Gaochun Civil Affairs Bureau is a proper litigation subject in this case and whether it can claim compensation from the appellees Wang Changsheng, Lü Fang, and Tianan Insurance Jiangsu Branch for the death of the unidentified deceased victim.

Opinion of the Court of Second Instance (Nanjing Intermediate People's Court):

The appellant Gaochun Civil Affairs Bureau is not a proper litigation subject in this case and has no right to claim personal injury compensation from the traffic accident against the appellees Wang Changsheng, Lü Fang, and Tianan Insurance Jiangsu Branch for the death of the unidentified deceased victim.

First, Article 108 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Civil Procedure Law) stipulates: "A lawsuit must meet the following conditions: (1) The plaintiff is a citizen, legal person, or other organization that has a direct interest in the case. ..." The "direct interest in the case" as provided herein refers to a civil rights-obligations relationship. Whether Gaochun Civil Affairs Bureau has a civil rights-obligations relationship with this case must be determined according to legal provisions. Firstly, according to the provisions of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Personal Injury Compensation Cases, where the victim dies, the compensation obligor shall compensate for funeral expenses, death compensation, etc. The same judicial interpretation also provides that the compensation claimant "refers to the victim who directly suffers personal injury due to the tort or other injurious cause, the person who is supported by the victim according to law, and the close relatives of the deceased victim." Accordingly, in personal injury compensation cases where the victim dies, the compensation claimants are the persons who are supported by the deceased victim according to law and the close relatives of the deceased victim. Gaochun Civil Affairs Bureau clearly does not fall within the category of "compensation claimants" as provided in this judicial interpretation and does not have the subject qualification to claim personal injury compensation from the appellees Wang Changsheng, Lü Fang, and Tianan Insurance Jiangsu Branch for the death of the unidentified deceased victim in this case. Secondly, Gaochun Civil Affairs Bureau failed to provide evidence during both the first and second instances that it had paid the funeral and related expenses for the unidentified deceased victim in this case, so it cannot be determined that a civil rights-obligations relationship exists between Gaochun Civil Affairs Bureau and the appellees Wang Changsheng, Lü Fang, and Tianan Insurance Jiangsu Branch. Therefore, Gaochun Civil Affairs Bureau has no direct interest in this case, and its lawsuit does not meet the requirements of Article 108(1) of the Civil Procedure Law.

Second, according to Articles 2, 4(1), 6(2), and 7 of the Measures for the Administration of Relief for City-Dwelling Vagrants and Beggars with No Means of Livelihood, the people's government of a city at or above the county level shall, as needed, establish relief stations for vagrants and beggars. The relief provided by relief stations to vagrants and beggars is a temporary social relief measure. The civil affairs department of the people's government at or above the county level is responsible for the relief work for vagrants and beggars and shall provide guidance and supervision to the relief stations. Relief stations shall promptly provide relief to persons seeking assistance who fall within the scope of relief targets and shall not refuse. Relief stations shall provide the following relief based on the needs of the recipients: (1) Providing food that meets food hygiene requirements; (2) Providing accommodation that meets basic conditions; (3) For those who suffer sudden acute illnesses within the station, promptly sending them to the hospital for treatment; (4) Assisting in contacting their relatives or work units; (5) For those who have no transportation expenses to return to their place of domicile or work unit, providing transportation vouchers. From the above provisions, it can be seen that the relief provided by civil affairs departments and relief stations to city-dwelling vagrants and beggars with no means of livelihood is a temporary relief measure. The content of the relief is to temporarily help vagrants and beggars solve their basic living needs. Their work duties do not include representing or substituting for such persons in filing civil lawsuits. The appellant Gaochun Civil Affairs Bureau's ground of appeal that its statutory relief duties include filing civil lawsuits on behalf of society's vagrants and beggars has no legal basis. Civil litigation arises between equal civil subjects. Gaochun Civil Affairs Bureau, as an administrative organ, intervening in civil litigation without legal authorization, is contrary to the fundamental principles of Chinese law.

Third, according to the provisions of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Personal Injury Compensation Cases, the compensation claimants in this case should be the persons who are supported by the unidentified deceased victim according to law and the close relatives of the unidentified deceased victim. In this case, although after the public security authorities published a notice in the newspaper, no compensation claimant for the unidentified deceased victim appeared up to the time of the first and second instances, the possibility that a compensation claimant exists objectively cannot be excluded. If a compensation claimant becomes aware of the circumstances of this case, they may still demand that the compensation obligor bear civil compensation liability according to law. The civil compensation liability that the appellees Wang Changsheng, Lü Fang, and Tianan Insurance Jiangsu Branch should bear according to law has not been completely extinguished.

In conclusion, the Nanjing Intermediate People's Court determined in the second instance that the appellant Gaochun Civil Affairs Bureau is not a proper litigation subject in this case, and its grounds of appeal lack legal basis and were not supported. The original court's ruling to dismiss the lawsuit of Gaochun Civil Affairs Bureau was not improper and should be affirmed. Pursuant to Article 108(1) and Article 154 of the Civil Procedure Law, on March 27, 2007, the Nanjing Intermediate People's Court ruled as follows:

The appeal is dismissed and the original ruling is affirmed.

The court acceptance fees for the first and second instances are RMB 50 each, totaling RMB 100, to be borne by the appellant Gaochun County Civil Affairs Bureau.

This ruling is final.
